definition: the means or opportunity to approach or make use of something
example: Everyone should have equal access to quality education.

definition: enough or satisfactory for a particular purpose
example: Many families struggle to find adequate housing in big cities.

definition: occurring once every year
example: The company holds an annual conference to review its progress.

definition: clearly visible or understood; obvious
example: It became apparent that the old policy was no longer effective.

definition: close to the actual number or size but not exact
example: The approximate cost of the project is two million dollars.

definition: a settled way of thinking or feeling about something
example: Public attitude toward remote work has changed significantly since the pandemic.

definition: to regard something as being caused by a particular factor
example: Experts attribute the rise in obesity partly to sedentary lifestyles.

definition: relating to ordinary citizens, as distinct from military or religious affairs
example: Civil rights movements have brought about major social change.

definition: a set of rules, or a system of symbols for communication
example: The company introduced a strict code of conduct for employees.

definition: to pledge or bind oneself to a course of action
example: The government has committed to reducing emissions by half.

definition: to share or exchange information with others
example: Effective leaders communicate clearly with their teams.

definition: to focus one's attention or efforts on something
example: Students often struggle to concentrate during long online lectures.

definition: to grant a title, benefit, or right, or to have discussions to reach a decision
example: A university degree confers certain advantages in the job market.

definition: a clear difference between two things when compared
example: There is a sharp contrast between urban and rural living standards.

definition: a series of events that repeat in the same order
example: Governments often struggle to break the cycle of poverty.

definition: a formal discussion of a topic with opposing viewpoints
example: There is ongoing debate about whether university education should be free.

definition: without being affected by; in spite of
example: Despite the high cost, many families still choose private education.

definition: an aspect or feature of a situation
example: Mental health adds another dimension to workplace well-being policies.

definition: relating to one's own country, or to the home
example: The government introduced measures to support domestic manufacturers.

definition: to become known or apparent
example: New evidence has emerged suggesting a link between diet and mental health.

definition: a mistake
example: Human error is responsible for the majority of workplace accidents.

definition: relating to a group of people with a shared cultural background
example: The city is home to a wide range of ethnic communities.

definition: an aim or desired result
example: One of the government's main goals is to reduce youth unemployment.

definition: a sum of money given for a particular purpose
example: The research team received a grant to study renewable energy storage.

definition: for this reason; therefore
example: The region has little rainfall, hence its dependence on irrigation.

definition: a proposed explanation based on limited evidence, used as a starting point for investigation
example: The researchers tested their hypothesis through a series of experiments.

definition: to put a plan or system into effect
example: The school plans to implement a new curriculum next year.

definition: to show that someone or something is involved in an event, especially a negative one
example: Poor diet has been implicated in a range of chronic illnesses.

definition: to force a rule, tax, or punishment onto someone
example: The government imposed stricter regulations on food advertising.

definition: to combine parts into a whole, or to include someone fully in a group
example: Schools should help integrate immigrant students into the community.

definition: existing or happening inside an organization or system
example: The company launched an internal investigation into the complaint.

definition: to carry out research or a systematic inquiry into something
example: Scientists are investigating the long-term effects of screen time on children.

definition: a paid position of regular employment
example: Automation could put millions of manufacturing jobs at risk.

definition: to describe or classify someone or something in a particular way
example: It is unfair to label all teenagers as lazy because of a few examples.

definition: a system or process by which something works or is achieved
example: The policy lacks a clear mechanism for measuring its success.

definition: easy to see or understand; clear
example: It is obvious that rising fuel prices affect the cost of almost everything.

definition: to fill or take up a space, position, or time
example: Housing costs occupy a growing share of household income.

definition: a choice available among several possibilities
example: Public transport is often the cheapest option for commuters.

definition: the amount of something produced
example: New machinery has significantly increased the factory's output.

definition: taking everything into account; total
example: The overall quality of healthcare has improved over the past decade.

definition: similar and happening at the same time; corresponding
example: There is a parallel between the rise of social media and increased anxiety among teens.

definition: a limit or boundary that defines the scope of something
example: The project was completed within the parameters set by the client.

definition: a distinct period or stage in a process
example: The first phase of the project focuses on research and planning.

definition: to say what will happen in the future based on evidence
example: Economists predict a slow but steady recovery next year.

definition: most important; main
example: The principal reason for the delay was a shortage of materials.

definition: existing or happening before something else
example: Applicants need prior experience in customer service.

definition: relating to a job that requires special skill or training
example: Professional development courses help employees stay up to date with new skills.

definition: a planned piece of work with a specific goal
example: The city launched a project to improve public transport links.

definition: to encourage or support something, or to raise someone to a higher rank
example: Schools should do more to promote healthy eating among students.

definition: a government, especially one considered strict, or a system of management
example: The country's political regime changed dramatically after the revolution.

definition: to find a solution to a problem or conflict
example: The two companies resolved their dispute through negotiation.

definition: to continue to have or keep something
example: Companies struggle to retain skilled employees without offering competitive pay.

definition: a number of things of the same kind coming one after another
example: The government introduced a series of reforms to boost the economy.

definition: a piece of numerical data collected for analysis
example: The statistic shows a sharp rise in online shopping since 2020.

definition: a person's or thing's position or standing relative to others
example: Employment status can significantly affect a person's access to credit.

definition: mental or emotional strain caused by demanding circumstances
example: Long working hours are a major cause of stress among employees.

definition: coming after something in time; following
example: The initial trial was successful, and subsequent tests confirmed the results.

definition: a quantity of money, or the total of numbers added together
example: The government spent a considerable sum on flood defenses.

definition: a brief statement of the main points of something
example: The report begins with a summary of the key findings.

definition: to commit to and begin a task or responsibility
example: The team will undertake a full review of the company's safety procedures.
